summary: This lecture tells of the start of the Prophet's open call around age 43, after three years of quiet calling to trusted people such as Ali and Abu Bakr. On Allah's command he invited his relatives to a meal twice, but Abu Lahab broke up the first gathering and only Ali answered the call at the second. He then climbed Mount Safa, asked whether they would believe him if told an army was behind the hill, and they said yes because he was As-Sadiq and Al-Amin, but Abu Lahab cursed him. Allah revealed Surah Al-Masad, and the ustaz explains the end of Abu Lahab and Umm Jamil and the harassment of the Prophet. The lecture closes with Sa'd shedding the first blood and the house of Al-Arqam as the centre of secret calling.
keyPoints: For three years the Prophet SAW called quietly to trusted people, helped by Abu Bakr.
Two banquets for his relatives failed, and only Ali answered his call.
On Mount Safa his people acknowledged him as As-Sadiq and Al-Amin, but Abu Lahab cursed him.
Surah Al-Masad was revealed about Abu Lahab and his wife Umm Jamil.
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was the first to shed blood in defence of the faith, then the house of Al-Arqam became the meeting place.

chapters.title: Umm Jamil cannot see the Prophet SAW
chapters.summary: The ustaz opens with Umm Jamil looking for Muzammam while Allah hid the Prophet SAW from her sight, then gives thanks for health and safety.

chapters.title: Three years of secret calling
chapters.summary: He called trusted people, received visitors from afar, and Abu Bakr found suitable people such as Abdurrahman and Uthman. Ali joined with Abu Talib's blessing.

chapters.title: The command and the two banquets
chapters.summary: Allah told him to convey the message to his relatives. Abu Lahab broke up the first banquet, and at the second only Ali declared he would follow.

chapters.title: To Mount Safa
chapters.summary: He looked for a place to address all of Mecca and climbed Mount Safa, the place for important announcements.

chapters.title: As-Sadiq and Al-Amin
chapters.summary: He asked whether they would believe an army was behind the hill, and they said yes because he was As-Sadiq, then he called them to leave idols.

chapters.title: Abu Lahab and Umm Jamil
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab was so called for his reddish face, and his wife Umm Jamil was known for her beauty.

chapters.title: Woe to you, Muhammad
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab cursed him because of the idol trade, and everyone left him, while the couple tormented him with thorns and rubbish.

chapters.title: Surah Al-Masad is revealed
chapters.summary: Allah revealed surah 111, short but very powerful, about Abu Lahab.

chapters.title: May Abu Lahab's hands perish
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab's wealth, as keeper of the Kaaba's donations, will not help him and he will enter a blazing fire.

chapters.title: The wife who carries firewood
chapters.summary: His wife, a troublemaker, will carry firewood, meaning she fuels hell's fire as she fuelled hostility on earth.

chapters.title: Umm Jamil and Muzammam
chapters.summary: Children sang the surah, so an angry Umm Jamil looked for Muzammam but could not see him beside Abu Bakr.

chapters.title: Abu Lahab's son and the lion
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab's son who spat at him was killed by a lion after the Prophet's supplication.

chapters.title: Abu Lahab rejoices at a child's death
chapters.summary: When the Prophet's son Abdullah died, Abu Lahab rejoiced and said Muhammad's line was cut off.

chapters.title: Abu Lahab's end and the broken engagements
chapters.summary: Abu Lahab died alone in disgrace, and had his sons break their engagements to Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum. Khadijah strengthened him.

chapters.title: Sa'd and the house of Al-Arqam
chapters.summary: Sa'd struck a harasser with a camel bone, and he chose the hidden house of Al-Arqam as the learning base.

chapters.title: Recap
chapters.summary: The ustaz recaps three years of secret calling up to Mount Safa, and gives thanks for the steadfastness of the Prophet and the companions.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions Allah commanding him to convey the message beginning with his nearest relatives.
May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.
dalil.translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined! May he be ruined too!

dalil.context: His wealth and gains will not avail him.
dalil.translation: Neither his wealth nor his gains will help him:

dalil.context: He will burn in a blazing fire.
dalil.translation: he will burn in the Flaming Fire––

dalil.context: And his wife, the carrier of firewood.
dalil.translation: and so will his wife, the firewood-carrier,

dalil.context: Around her neck is a rope of twisted fibre.
dalil.translation: with a palm-fibre rope around her neck.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions Surah Al-Kawthar, to be told later, on Abu Lahab's claim that he was cut off.
dalil.translation: We have truly given abundance to you [Prophet]––

The Prophet SAW climbed Mount Safa, called his people and asked whether they would believe him if told an army was behind the hill. They said yes, so he warned them of punishment, and Abu Lahab cursed him.
dalil.context: The ustaz narrates this event. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.context: Known for her beauty and for inciting opposition to the Prophet SAW, and Allah hid him from her sight.
Found people fit to receive Islam and sat beside the Prophet SAW when Umm Jamil came.
Told Ali to follow Muhammad but did not accept Islam himself.

people.role: The child who answered the call
people.context: Welcomed guests at the banquet and the only one to declare he would follow the Prophet SAW.
Invited by Abu Bakr to embrace Islam.
Invited by Abu Bakr to embrace Islam.

people.context: Broke up the banquet, cursed him on Mount Safa and kept the Kaaba's donation box. Surah Al-Masad was revealed about him.
Spat at him and was later killed by a lion after his supplication.
Encouraged him when he was reviled.
The reason he was called Abul Qasim.
Died young and Abu Lahab rejoiced.
Betrothed to Abu Lahab's son before Islam.
Betrothed to Abu Lahab's son before Islam.

people.role: A young man with a hidden house
people.context: His house became the centre for Muslims to learn and gather.

sirah.era: From secret to open calling (age 40 to 43)
sirah.summary: This lecture covers three years of secret calling, the family banquets, the call at Mount Safa, Surah Al-Masad and the house of Al-Arqam.

events.label: Banquet
events.title: The first banquet is broken up
events.desc: Abu Lahab stood up and left before he could speak.

events.label: Ali
events.title: Only Ali responds
events.desc: At the second banquet all were silent and Ali said he would follow.

events.label: Safa
events.title: The call on Mount Safa
events.desc: He called all of Mecca and Abu Lahab cursed him.

events.label: Masad
events.title: Surah Al-Masad is revealed
events.desc: Allah revealed a surah about Abu Lahab and his wife.

events.label: Unseen
events.title: Umm Jamil cannot see him
events.desc: Allah hid him from her sight as she looked for him.

events.label: Lion
events.title: Abu Lahab's son is killed by a lion
events.desc: The lion pounced only on the son who had spat at him.

events.label: Blood
events.title: Sa'd sheds the first blood
events.desc: Sa'd struck a harasser disturbing prayer with a camel bone.

events.label: Al-Arqam
events.title: The house of Al-Arqam is chosen
events.desc: The hidden house became the centre for learning and worship.

lessons.title: Calling in stages
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW called secretly first before being commanded to do so openly.

lessons.title: Allah protects His Messenger
lessons.body: Allah hid the Prophet from Umm Jamil's sight so she could not see him.

lessons.title: Honesty acknowledged by all
lessons.body: His people acknowledged him as As-Sadiq, never lying, and Al-Amin, the trusted.

lessons.title: Wealth does not save
lessons.body: Abu Lahab's wealth could not help him against punishment.

lessons.title: Do not fuel hostility
lessons.body: Abu Lahab's wife is pictured carrying firewood because she fuelled hostility.

lessons.title: Offering condolences to the bereaved
lessons.body: We offer condolences and pray for patience, not rejoice as Abu Lahab did.

lessons.title: A wife who strengthens
lessons.body: Khadijah encouraged him to keep going out to call people.

lessons.title: Not giving up
lessons.body: Because he did not give up, we know Islam today.

lessons.title: Appreciating the companions' sacrifice
lessons.body: The companions endured hardship so we can utter the shahada.

glossary.meaning: A hill in Mecca where important announcements were made.
The truthful, a title of the Prophet SAW.
The trustworthy, with whom people kept valuables.
Father of flame, for his reddish face.
The reviled, Umm Jamil's mocking name for Muhammad.
The house of Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam, the Muslims' secret learning centre.
